articles.title: B/R Staff Predictions for UFC 333 Main Card
articles.summary: UFC 333 is right around the corner, and it is one of the deepest cards of the year on paper, with elite talent from the bottom of the bill to the top.
articles.body:
UFC 333 is right around the corner, and it is one of the deepest cards of the year on paper, with elite talent from the bottom of the bill to the top.

The main event will see featherweight legend Alexander Volkanovski attempt to defend his belt against Movsar Evloev, who has yet to be beaten in 20 professional fights.

There will also be a title up for grabs in the co-main event, as bantamweight champ Petr Yan takes on challenger Merab Dvalishvili. It will be the third time the two bantamweight greats have met in the Octagon, after splitting their first two meetings 1-1.

The remainder of the main card will be packed with exciting contenders. That includes a flyweight fight between top-10 talents Lone'er Kavanagh and Ramazan Temirov, a heavyweight showdown between hulking Russians Alexander Volkov and Rizvan Kuniev, and a featherweight scrap between proven finishers Losene Keita and Aaron Pico.

It has the makings of a very exciting night of MMA.

Here's how the B/R combat sports team sees it all going down.

Adam Kramer: The oddsmakers essentially see this as a coin flip , which feels about right. And given their contrasting styles, this feels like one of the more unique MMA chess matches in recent memory.

That said, we know what each fighter would like to do. Volkanovski wants to strike, and he wants to rely on incredible footwork and technique to do so. Evloev wants to clinch, wrestle, and ultimately bring the fight to the ground.

Thus far, that style has worked for the challenger. He's 20-0, after all. It's not the sexiest way to win, but Evloev is a real threat, and he's showcased that against an incredible lineup of fighters over his past five fights.

Volkanovski recovered nicely after back-to-back losses with two wins, albeit both coming over Diego Lopes. Still, he's 38 years old and likely to be pushed at a frantic pace unless he can end this fight early.

This one doesn't have to be all that complicated. If they stay standing, Volk wins. If Evloev makes it ugly, he likely does enough to win by decision. I believe he'll do that, even if Volkanovski threatens throughout. What a fun matchup.

Prediction: Evloev by unanimous decision

Tom Taylor: Movsar Evloev's record is pretty darn shiny, but I suspect it will be tarnished at the hands of Alexander Volkanovski this weekend.

The champ himself has given a pretty good assessment of this matchup, I think. He believes the only way Evloev beats him is by catching him somehow, and given that the challenger has not scored a finish in 10 straight fights—on the feet or on the mat—it's very hard to see that happening.

Yes, Evloev has the wrestling and cardio to potentially win a decision, but Volkanovski was able to hang with Islam Makhachev in the grappling, and Makhachev, who is now the welterweight champ, is way bigger and way better than Evloev.

Long story short, Evloev is unlikely to show Volkanovski anything he hasn't seen before, and he doesn't have the firepower or killer instinct to surprise the champ. Volkanovski sets the terms of the fight and wins a clear decision.

Prediction: Volkanovski by unanimous decision

Lyle Fitzsimmons: If you're a UFC fan, you're probably an Alex fan. In fact, I was driving in my car yesterday, heard "Down Under" on the radio, and immediately thought of the last time I was in a building for one of his ring walks. Quite the spectacle.

Volkanovski reinvented himself – thanks to Diego Lopes – after he was splattered by Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria, but at 38 years old and with another hungry lion charging, can he keep the Aussie mojo going?

The guess here is no. I don't foresee a pretty fight or a particularly fan-friendly one. But Evloev has shown he can get top-end guys down and keep them there. That's not great news for the fans. And it'd be even worse news for Volkanovski.

Adam Kramer: Why should this fight go different than the one we saw back in December? It's a fair place to begin.

As shocking as it was, the formula to stop Dvalishvili wasn't all that complicated. Yan's takedown defense was superb in that fight, and he seemed to break his opponent even more as the night went on.

Still, Merab fought four times last year. In his fight against Yan, it showed. And for the first time in a long time, he looked gassed.

A long layoff was needed for Merab, and it should do him extraordinarily well. How he changes his game plan will be fascinating to watch, as will Yan's adjustments following such a dominant win last time they fought.

Merab, now a decent-sized underdog, will be better conditioned. And the attempts to bring this down to the mat should be different this time around. Maybe doubting Yan given everything we saw between these two less than a year ago will be a mistake, but it's one we're willing to try.

A rested Merab will prove to be a much more functional Merab.

Tom Taylor: I was very confident Merab Dvalishvili would beat Petr Yan last time they fought. I was very wrong about that, and I won't make the same mistake again.

While I consider Dvalishvili the best bantamweight of all time, Yan really seemed to figure him out last time—figure him out in a way that will be difficult to undo. He stopped takedowns, weathered Dvalishvili's non-stop aggression, and fired back with heavy artillery from bell to bell. I see no reason why he won't be able to do something similar again.

I agree that Dvalishvili will probably be well rested and better prepared this time around, but I really don't see what changes he can implement to beat the Yan that showed up when they last met.

I'm calling for a repeat of the second fight. It'll be reasonably close, but Yan will once again get the win after five fun rounds.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Simple question. From which fight do you pull the most evidence?

The first one, when a pre-reign Dvalishvili scored 11 takedowns and nearly seven minutes of control time? Or the second, in which he was denied on all but two of his takedown tries while Yan mixed his own striking attack to the head, body, and legs?

Prediction: Dvalishvili by unanimous decision

Adam Kramer: The Kavanagh hype was upended back in July against Brandon Royval, and there's no shame in that. Royval has done that to others before and remains a matchup nightmare regardless of the opponent.

In terms of style, Temirov will be much different. Kavanagh's biggest worry here, first and foremost, should be power rather than submission. Temirov has ended four of his last five fights in the first round and two of those wins came in the first 60 seconds.

That could be an issue for Kavanagh, who has been finished in two of his last three fights.

Granted, he's a superb fighter with a significant reach advantage. Taking advantage of that reach will be critical, as it will allow him to avoid trouble.

The problem is that the power difference is enormous. And in terms of the fight outcome, it just feels like that could ultimately be the deciding factor.

Tom Taylor: This is a really hard fight to call, and it's almost impossible to feel confident about the outcome either way.

That said, I'm going to go with Lone'er Kavanagh. There's definitely a huge risk he'll be finished by Ramazan Temirov, who is both extremely aggressive and absurdly powerful for the flyweight division, but I think he is smart enough to be cautious and use his range and cardio to control the action after his opponent's initial assault.

He may never be champ, but I don't place too much stock in his loss to Brandon Royval. He's still clearly very good. Good enough, I believe, to win this fight on points.

Prediction: Kavanagh by unanimous decision

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Who imposes his will, or at least his fighting style, on the other guy?

Can Kavanagh bounce back from two losses in his last three fights – both inside the distance – or are the losses to Charles Johnson and Brandon Royval indications that he doesn't belong at the highest level?

Temirov is certainly a challenge, given that he beat Johnson and blew away former title challenger Steve Erceg, and it says here that it's too much for Kavanagh to handle.

Adam Kramer: Let's start with the height and reach advantages, which are pretty much where every fight featuring Volkov should start. At 6'7", he'll be three inches taller and have a four-inch reach advantage over Kuniev, who will do everything possible to close the distance and make this fight ugly.

It's the right plan, although Volkov could very well be up for it. In fact, it's remarkable how good he has been over his last five fights, which include four wins and one split-decision loss against Ciryl Gane.

He's fought grapplers, he's fought balanced fighters, and he's fought heavy-handed fighters like Sergei Pavlovich. Volkov's measurements and style have proven to be a challenge for just about everyone, and it feels like that will be the case once again.

Kuniev will do his best to break the rhythm, but it won't be enough.

Prediction: Volkov by unanimous decision

Tom Taylor: Outside of Tom Aspinall, whose future in the sport is very uncertain at the moment, there is no heavyweight in the UFC I'd pick to beat Volkov right now. Years after his brief reign as Bellator heavyweight champ, and after some serious inconsistency, the towering Russian has seemingly found his groove. He's beaten everyone the UFC has put in front of him in recent years, with the exception of an absolute robbery against Ciryl Gane. I can't see that changing on Saturday. Rizvan Kuniev has looked decent in the UFC, scraping by Jailton Almeida and knocking out Tyrell Fortune in his two Octagon wins, but neither of those performances was particularly mind-blowing, and neither opponent is anywhere near Volkov's level.

Volkov's experience at the highest level will carry him to victory in this one. Kuniev is unlikely to give him any new looks, which will allow him to use his range to cruise to a wide decision—maybe even a late stoppage.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Every time I play the "yeah, sure, Volkov is tall, but (opponent name goes here) can do this, this, and this to him in spite of the size differential." And then I'm wrong.

It's been that way for five years, beyond losses to guys named Ciryl Gane and Tom Aspinall.

I appreciate how good Kuniev is and how he's only lost (by a narrow decision) once in the last 10 years. But I'm not getting fooled again. At least not the way I have been.

Adam Kramer: The whole notion that "styles make fights" might be tiring to some, although it feels appropriate here. And there's something beautiful in MMA when two fighters find enormous success through two very different routes.

For Keita, he wants to be upright. He wants to strike. He wants to end this fight early, which he has done 11 of his 17 wins. If this doesn't go to the mat, Keita has an enormous advantage.

For Pico, who will be fighting in his third UFC fight after an impressive Bellator run, wrestling will certainly be part of his strategy.

He has heavy hands, and he will use them at times. Although his strong wrestling background coupled with his opponent should make the strategy somewhat simplified here. And that wrestling and grappling should be put to use early and often.

Pico will pick his spots, avoid the big shot and that will be enough.

Tom Taylor: At his best, Aaron Pico is one of the most technically proficient and naturally gifted fighters I've ever seen. His recent win over Patricio "Pitbull" Freire was evidence of this. He looked incredible in the Octagon that night. Near perfect.

That said, I really don't like this matchup for him. On paper, he has all the tools to win—namely his elite wrestling, which we don't often see in his fights. Unfortunately, he is prone to throwing caution to the wind, which almost never works out for him, because he is one of the least durable fighters in the sport. Against a knockout artist like Keita, that could be a huge problem.

This is such a weird matchup, because if Pico fights to his potential, he should win very easily, but it's just hard to trust him to do that.

I see him starting strong, slipping into autopilot, and walking into something that puts him out. I don't want it to happen that way, but I have a feeling that's how it will go down.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Pico is one of what seems like a bunch of recent guys who did great things at Bellator only to arrive at the UFC and fall immediately short.

His fight with Patricio Pitbull in April was a showdown of two of those guys, in fact.

But there's still a lot to like with Pico, particularly given his not-so-advanced age (30) and what seems like a favorable style matchup here.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez's super-middleweight world title fight with Christian Mbilli still set to go on in Riyadh despite conflict
articles.summary: Canelo Alvarez's fight with Christian Mbilli for the WBC title is still set to go ahead in Riyadh on October 31; Riyadh's airport was bombed earlier this month and other sports events in Riyadh have been postponed; But Mbilli's promoter said: "I'm very confident the fight goes ahead"
articles.body:
Riyadh's King Khalid airport has been bombed in recent days during the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

The UK government is warning against non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia, the US advises citizens to reconsider travel there.

Despite those risks the show currently looks set to go ahead.

Mbilli isn't backing down. His promoter Camille Estephan told Sky Sports : "Christian will arrive in Saudi as planned.

"I'm very confident the fight goes ahead and Mbilli will keep his belt and dethrone Canelo, God willing."

It's a significant fight for Canelo. It will be his first bout since Terence Crawford defeated him in a spectacular performance in 2025.

When Crawford retired the super-middleweight titles scattered.

Canada's Mbilli is undefeated, winning the WBC interim 168lb belt when he beat Maciej Sulecki. He retained the strap when he drew with Lester Martinez last year. He was then upgraded to full world championship status when Crawford vacated the title.

Mexican superstar Canelo, looking to come back with a win and reclaim his old title, has boxed in Riyadh once before, a unanimous points win over William Scull.

Other sports events, like tennis' Six Kings Slam, that were due to take place in Riyadh have been postponed.

articles.title: Mayweather quiere encontrar al único boxeador que le venció para ayudarlo: “Está sin hogar”
articles.standfirst: 'Money' habla en PBD Podcast de una posible revancha con McGregor, de los más de 500 millones que le han estafado y de un antiguo y desaparecido rival
articles.summary: 'Money' habla en PBD Podcast de una posible revancha con McGregor, de los más de 500 millones que le han estafado y de un antiguo y desaparecido rival
articles.body: Floyd Mayweather ha intervenido en PBD Podcast de Youtube y allí ha hablado de diferentes temas, como su posible revancha con Conor McGregor o su situación financiera. Ha reconocido que gran parte de su fortuna se esfumó, pues personas en las que confiaba le robaron más de 500 millones de dólares. "Un hombre que era algo así como una figura paterna para mí me robó 350 millones de dólares. Me estaba ayudando y yo creía que era mi amigo. Años después empezamos a revisar la documentación y descubrimos que había desaparecido el dinero", ha confesado Floyd. Esta no fue la única supuesta estafa que sufrió ‘Pretty Boy’ según ha explicado: “Había un hombre que se hacía pasar por mi amigo, que me ayudaba a poner en orden mis negocios y me robó 200 millones de dólares más". El expúgil, sin embargo, admite: “Nací pobre, puedo caer hasta el fondo, pero puedo volver a la cima. Sé cómo escalar, la mierda pasa. Sigo viviendo muy bien". Actualmente el excampeón está en litigios con Al Haymon y Stephen Espinoza, dos de los hombres clave en la vida financiera de Mayweather. Sea como fuere, ‘Money’ mantiene su interés en organizar peleas de exhibición para ganar dinero y el nombre de Conor McGregor salió a colación: “Creo que Conor McGregor y yo podríamos volver a pelear. Sí, absolutamente. No vivo con Conor McGregor, no es mi amigo, no tengo que verlo. Simplemente, cuando llegue el momento de hacer negocios y pelear, hagámoslo". Hay un nombre que quizás nadie esperaba y del que también se habló: Serafim Todorov, el último boxeador que venció a Mayweather, concretamente en las semifinales de los Juegos Olímpicos de Atlanta en 1996. "En realidad, el tipo con el que perdí, creo que ahora está sin hogar, por lo que me han dicho. Todo pasa por una razón, pero no le deseo el mal a nadie. Si puedo encontrarlo y darle dinero o prestarle ayuda, no hay problema", dijo el expúgil de 49 años. El presentador de PBD Podcast (Patrick Bet-David), preguntó: "¿Lo harías?" A lo que Floyd respondió: “Absolutamente”; PBD replicó: “¿Qué tal si me dejas ir a buscarlo? Lo voy a encontrar”. Lanzado el guante, cabe recordar que el búlgaro Serafim Todorov (57 años) fue tres veces campeón del mundo amateur, pero desde que ganó aquella medalla de plata en Atlanta su carrera y su vida ya fueron cuesta abajo. Intentó competir en los Juegos de Sídney bajo nacionalidad turca, que le pagaba un buen dinero por representarlos, pero esa idea naufragó. Se acabó haciendo profesional y tuvo una carrera corta e intrascendente. Dejó el pugilismo y comenzó a trabajar en cualquier cosa que le salía. Tuvo problemas con el alcohol y aseguró que le ofrecieron trabajo en el crimen organizado, camino que rechazó. Lo último que se supo de él, hace ya más de una década, es que vivía con una ayuda estatal de menos de 500 euros al mes para él y su familia.

images.caption: Floyd Mayweather durante su entrevista en PBD Podcast.

articles.title: Manny Pacquiao Fight on Tyson Fury-Joshua Card Agreed to by Joe Cordina, Latest Details Revealed
articles.summary: It sounds like boxing legend Manny Pacquiao could be in action later this year.
articles.body:
It sounds like boxing legend Manny Pacquiao could be in action later this year.

Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn told BoxingScene.com that Joe Cordina has "agreed terms to face Pacquiao, but we don't know if it's happening. From our side, we've agreed to do it." The fight would take place on the Dec. 11 Netflix card headlined by heavyweight legends Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

A two-time IBF super-featherweight champion, Cordina would be in the biggest fight of his career if Pacquiao agrees to terms. The 19-1 slugger most recently fought in December, earning a unanimous decision win over Gabriel Flores Jr. in his second appearance since moving back up to lightweight.

At 47 years old, Pacquiao is still one of the biggest names in boxing. He returned to the ring after a four-year hiatus in July 2025, fighting WBC welterweight champion Mario Barrios to a draw. His impressive performance fueled optimism that he could continue his boxing career despite his age.

Earlier this year, it was announced that Pacquiao would face Floyd Mayweather Jr. in a rematch of their iconic 2015 clash. However, the fight was postponed indefinitely after Mayweather was sued for breach of contract.

While there would be a significant age difference against the 34-year-old Cordina, the allure of being on the biggest boxing card of the year could be tough for Pacquiao to turn down. Fury and Joshua have been building towards their showdown for over a decade, so their main event would certainly draw a large audience.

Adding Pacquiao to the card would boost the fan interest even further, so many will be keeping their fingers crossed that he agrees to face Cordina.

articles.title: Who is Alexander Volkov? Meet the UFC heavyweight contender known as Drago who is set to fight at UFC 333
articles.summary: Alexander Volkov is a Russian mixed martial artist who competes in the UFC heavyweight division.
articles.body: Alexander Volkov is a Russian mixed martial artist who competes in the UFC heavyweight division. Known by his nickname “Drago,” he has established himself as one of the division’s most experienced fighters. He is a former heavyweight champion in both Bellator MMA and M-1 Global.Standing 6 feet 7 inches tall, Volkov is known for his powerful striking, technical boxing and impressive reach. He has earned major victories over former champions and top contenders, including Fabricio Werdum, Alistair Overeem and Sergei Pavlovich. As of now, he is ranked No. 4 in the Meta UFC heavyweight rankings.Who is Alexander Volkov?Alexander Yevgenyevich Volkov was born on October 24, 1988, in Moscow, Russia. He began his professional MMA career in April 2009. He soon developed a reputation as a dangerous heavyweight. He won his first two fights by technical knockout before suffering his first professional defeat by submission.Volkov continued improving and competed in several promotions before reaching international prominence. In 2012, he joined Bellator MMA and entered its heavyweight tournament. He defeated Brett Rogers and Vinicius Queiroz before beating Richard Hale by unanimous decision to win the Bellator Heavyweight Championship in December 2012.His first title reign ended in November 2013 when Vitaly Minakov stopped him in the first round. Volkov bounced back by winning the Bellator Season 10 heavyweight tournament in 2014. However, consecutive losses to Tony Johnson and Cheick Kongo in 2015 led to his departure from the promotion.Volkov later returned to M-1 Global and captured its heavyweight championship in February 2016. He defended the title successfully against former Bellator light heavyweight champion Attila Vegh later that year.The Russian fighter signed with the UFC in September 2016. He made his promotional debut against Timothy Johnson in November, winning by split decision. He then defeated Roy Nelson and Stefan Struve before producing one of the biggest victories of his career.In March 2018, Volkov knocked out former UFC heavyweight champion Fabricio Werdum in the fourth round. The performance earned him a Performance of the Night bonus and strengthened his position among the division’s leading contenders.In 2023, Volkov submitted Tai Tuivasa with an Ezekiel choke, becoming only the second fighter in UFC history to finish a fight using that technique. He also defeated Sergei Pavlovich by unanimous decision in June 2024.Volkov narrowly lost a controversial split decision to Ciryl Gane in December 2024. He returned to winning ways against Jailton Almeida in October 2025 and Waldo Cortes-Acosta in May 2026.With 40 wins and 11 losses in 51 professional fights, Volkov has recorded 24 knockout victories, four submission wins and 12 decision victories. His upcoming fight against Rizvan Kuniev is scheduled for October 24, 2026, at UFC 333.Volkov trains with Strela Team and holds a black belt in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, along with a third-dan black belt in Tsu Shin Gen.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Joe Cordina agrees terms to face great Manny Pacquiao in Cardiff
articles.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn says former world champion Joe Cordina has agreed terms to face boxing great Manny Pacquiao on the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard.
articles.body:
Boxing great Manny Pacquiao, 47, could be added to the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard - with former world champion Joe Cordina having agreed terms as his opponent.

Fury and Joshua are set to meet in an all-British heavyweight battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.

Now promoter Eddie Hearn has confirmed that negotiations for a mouth-watering fight on the undercard are at an advanced stage.

"We've agreed terms to face Pacquiao, but we don't know if it's happening," Hearn revealed at a media event on Thursday.

Tickets for Fury-Joshua sold out in just one hour, and fight fans could now also be able to see iconic eight-weight world champion Pacquiao face Wales' former super-featherweight world champion Cordina.

Pacquiao is regarded as one of the best boxers of all time, and it would be the first time the 12-time former champion has fought in the UK.

Details of other fights on the eagerly anticipated clash are yet to be released.

The compromises and power struggles that shaped Fury-Joshua

Ex-boxing world champion Joe Cordina cleared of assault after petrol station punch

Pacquiao has not fought since July 2025, having returned from his second attempt at retirement.

But the Filipino icon would still be a draw for the huge television audience expected for the fight, that will be broadcast globally by streaming giants Netflix.

But the emergence of Cardiff-born Cordina, 34, as an opponent will also provide a hometown flavour to the show.

A former IBF super-featherweight champion, Cordina had been scheduled to face American Abduallah Mason for the WBO lightweight title in Cleveland in July when he was denied a US visa.

Cordina had remained in training while standing trial for allegations of assault, eventually being cleared of all charges .

That verdict has paved the way for a place on the Joshua-Fury bill, with Cordina eager to resume his career on what would be a huge opportunity in his own city.

It would be the first time Pacquiao has faced a British opponent since he beat Ricky Hatton in Las Vegas in 2009.

Pacquiao's last fight was a failed bid to take Mario Barrios' welterweight title, the bout ending in a majority draw four years after retiring to focus on politics in is homeland.

He has a record of 62 wins from 73 fights and had been scheduled to face unbeaten Floyd Mayweather in September, but the rematch of their 2015 meeting was postponed indefinitely in June.

Cordina has previously fought on the undercard of Fury's first fight with Oleksandr Usyk, losing his IBF title to Belfast's Anthony Cacace in Riyadh in May 2024.

It would represent the former Olympian's first fight in Cardiff since he regained the belt against Shavkat Rahimov the previous year.

articles.title: David Benavidez, Vergil Ortiz Jr. championship doubleheader official for December
articles.summary: Benavidez, the unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion, will fight Polish WBC titlist Michal Cieslak on Dec. 5. And in the co-feature, Ortiz will end a 13...
articles.body:
Two of boxing's most exciting fighters, David Benavidez and Vergil Ortiz Jr., will be sharing the stage later this year.

Benavidez, the unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion, will fight Polish WBC titlist Michal Cieslak on Dec. 5 at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. And in the co-feature, Ortiz will end a 13-month layoff against former champion Keith Thurman.

The pay-per-view doubleheader will be available on DAZN and Amazon Prime Video, and it will also be part of the DAZN Ultimate subscription.

Benavidez (32-0, 26 KOs), a three-division world champion, surged through the pound-for-pound rankings in May after his impressive sixth-round destruction of Gilberto "Zurdo" Ramirez.

Cieslak (28-2, 22 KOs) captured the WBC interim title by stopping Jean Pascal in June 2025. He hasn't fought since, but he received the biggest news of his career when he was upgraded to full champion in September after Noel Mikaelian's title was stripped.

Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs) is the WBC interim super welterweight champion, but his Dec. 12 fight with Thurman will be contested at the middleweight limit — and it is expected Ortiz will continue his career at 160 pounds.

Ortiz was last in action when he knocked out Erickson Lubin in two rounds last November. He was in negotiations to face Jaron "Boots" Ennis in one of boxing's most anticipated fights, but Ortiz found himself tangled in a legal battle with his promoter, Oscar De La Hoya's Golden Boy, instead.

Ortiz and Golden Boy ultimately settled and agreed to complete the three fights remaining on their promotional deal beginning in December.

Thurman (31-2, 23 KOs), a former unified welterweight champion, is looking to bounce back from his one-sided KO defeat to WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian Fundora in March. Thurman, 37, has been inactive in the last few years and has not recorded a significant win since his unanimous decision victory over Mario Barrios in February 2022. He will be a heavy underdog against Ortiz.

articles.title: Eddie Alvarez net worth 2026: How the Underground King built his fortune across MMA, his UFC career, wins and more
articles.summary: Eddie Alvarez is one of the most accomplished lightweight fighters of his generation.
articles.body: Eddie Alvarez is one of the most accomplished lightweight fighters of his generation. Known as “The Underground King,” he became a champion in Bellator and the UFC during a career that spanned more than two decades.Alvarez built his reputation through high-level fights against some of MMA’s biggest names. He defeated Michael Chandler, Shinya Aoki, Anthony Pettis, Rafael dos Anjos and Justin Gaethje. He later moved into bare-knuckle boxing and continued competing at a high level.What is Eddie Alvarez’ net worth in 2026As of 2026, Eddie Alvarez has an estimated net worth of $8 million (per celebrity net worth). His wealth has come from his long MMA career, championship fights, bonuses, sponsorships and major contracts outside the UFC.Alvarez became Bellator’s first Lightweight Champion in 2009. He later regained the title after losing it to Michael Chandler in their famous 2011 fight. Their 2013 rematch ended with Alvarez winning by split decision.His biggest career breakthrough came after joining the UFC in 2014. Alvarez defeated Gilbert Melendez and Anthony Pettis before facing Rafael dos Anjos for the UFC Lightweight Championship in July 2016.Alvarez stopped dos Anjos in the first round to become UFC champion. He became the first fighter to win both the Bellator and UFC lightweight titles.His reign lasted only four months. At UFC 205, Alvarez faced Conor McGregor at Madison Square Garden. McGregor stopped him in the second round and became the first simultaneous two-division UFC champion.Alvarez still earned significant money during his UFC career. His disclosed purse for his UFC debut against Donald Cerrone was $100,000. He received another $100,000 for his win over Pettis and $150,000 for defeating dos Anjos. He also received a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus for the championship victory.After leaving the UFC in 2018, Alvarez signed with ONE Championship. He described the agreement as a guaranteed eight-figure package. That meant the deal was worth at least $10 million, although the exact amount he eventually received was never disclosed.His ONE Championship run produced one win, two losses and one no contest. He later moved to Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship.Alvarez defeated former UFC title challenger Chad Mendes by split decision in his BKFC debut in 2023. He then lost to Mike Perry before facing Jeremy Stephens in Philadelphia in 2025.Alvarez finished his professional MMA career with a record of 30 wins, eight losses and two no contests. His résumé includes victories over several former champions and elite contenders.Eddie Alvarez’ personal life His success also transformed his personal life. Alvarez grew up in Philadelphia’s Kensington neighborhood and began boxing at a young age. Before MMA became financially successful, he worked construction while supporting his family.He and his wife, Jamie, have four children. articles.title: Watch Arman Tsarukyan, Dillon Danis Brawl in Chaotic Video Ahead of RAF 14 Fight
articles.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Dillon Danis were involved in a brawl ahead of their freestyle wrestling match at RAF 14 in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Arman Tsarukyan and Dillon Danis were involved in a brawl ahead of their freestyle wrestling match at RAF 14 in Las Vegas.

After Danis showed off a shirt that called out Khamzat Chimaev, who will be facing Robbie Lawler in the co-main event of RAF 14, Tsarukyan crossed the stage to confront his opponent.

Changes WWE Needs for WrestleMania 43 🛠️

It sparked a scuffle between their teams, which left a security guard bleeding.

It's understandable why the shirt caused an issue, as Tsarukyan and Chimaev have become friends while training with each other.

Tsarukyan was also part of Chimaev's camp for his clash with Dricus Du Plessis at UFC 319.

Chimaev previously faced Danis at an RAF show on June 13, with a massive brawl breaking out after Chimaev secured a quick pin.

Tsarukyan, who also owns a 24-3-0 record in the UFC, holds a 7-1 record in his RAF career and is coming off a loss to Colby Covington in July.

He'll face Tsarukyan at Fontainebleau in Las Vegas on Friday.

articles.summary: The Ultimate Fighting Championship is returning to Abu Dhabi on Oct. 24.
articles.body:
The Ultimate Fighting Championship returns to Abu Dhabi on Oct.24. Here's how to watch the event.

UFC 333 on Paramount+: US start times for Volkanovski vs.Evloev and Yan vs. Dvalishvili 3

The UFC 333 early prelims will stream live in the U.S. on UFC FightPass and Paramount+ beginning at 10 a.m. ET/7 a.m. PT. Paramount+will carry the prelims at noon ET/9 a.m. PT, followed by the maincard at 2 p.m. ET/11 a.m. PT. Alexander Volkanovski (28-4) defends his featherweight titleagainst Movsar Evloev (20-0) in the main event. Volkanovski beganhis second reign by defeating Diego Lopes for the vacant championship last year and has since defended it ina rematch against Lopes. Evloev enters his first UFC title fightwith 10 promotional victories. Petr Yan (20-5) defends his bantamweight championship against MerabDvalishvili (21-5) in the co-main event, their third meeting.Dvalishvili won their first fight in 2023, captured the title thefollowing year and made three successful defenses before facing Yanagain last December. Yan reclaimed the belt by unanimous decision,repeatedly defending takedowns and landing effective strikes.

How to watch UFC 333 in the United Kingdom

Fans in the U.K. and Ireland can watch UFC 333 on TNT Sports, withstreaming available through HBO Max. The early prelims begin at 3p.m. BST on Saturday, Oct. 24, followed by the prelims at 5 p.m.and the main card at 7 p.m. The early prelims are also available onUFC Fight Pass. articles.title: Filip Hrgovic on course for title defence against Frank Sanchez in Croatia before a unification with Daniel Dubois
articles.summary: IBF heavyweight world champion Filip Hrgovic looks to be on course for a mandatory title defence against Frank Sanchez next; He's likely to have a homecoming bout in Croatia next against Sanchez; Hrgovic's hopes of an immediate unification with WBO champ Daniel Dubois are on hold
articles.body:
Hrgovic won the IBF heavyweight world championship when he scored an upset stoppage win over Moses Itauma in August.

He was ringside on Saturday at The O2 arena to watch Daniel Dubois defend his WBO heavyweight championship and even faced off with the Londoner.

But rather than an immediate unification with Dubois, Hrgovic looks set to make a mandatory IBF title defence against Frank Sanchez in Croatia.

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports : "I expect Frank Sanchez versus Filip Hrgovic to take place in the first quarter of 2027, perhaps in Zagreb, but too early to know for sure."

He continued: "I have already communicated with George Warren [of Queensberry promotions] and will likely speak again this week. Frank has speed and power, but also brings experience and stamina, so he is anxious to fight Hrgovic.

"[Sanchez's trainer] Eddie Reynoso loves the match and so do I. Sanchez will become the first Cuban heavyweight champion."

Zagreb is a potential location for the Hrgovic-Sanchez fight and the local arena has welcomed the possibility.

Sretan Saric, the manager director of Arena Zagreb, told Sky Sports : "Of course I support the opportunity to hold the fight at Arena Zagreb."

Dubois has previously beaten Hrgovic but will be open to boxing the Croatian once again.

"To win all the belts. That's the main thing now for me, collecting all the other belts," he previously told Sky Sports .

"It would mean everything to have all those belts. No one can take that away from me. That's what I'm after now.

"Any one of them, Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or [WBC champion Agit] Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… Anyone who wants it."

articles.title: Video: Khamzat Restrained During RAF Brawl — ‘I’ll F—k You Up Bro!‘
articles.summary: Real American Freestyle (RAF) is ostensibly a wrestling promotion, but where they really excel is brawls, scuffles, and brouhahas. The latest commotion occur...
articles.body:
Real American Freestyle (RAF) is ostensibly a wrestling promotion, but where they really excel is brawls, scuffles, and brouhahas .

The latest commotion occurred on Thursday at the RAF 14 pre-fight press conference. Predictably, the chaos was centered around jiu-jitsu black belt and frequent nuisance Dillon Danis , who really has no other reason to be on a wrestling mat but to cause trouble. Danis unveiled his shirt that read "Khamzat is my b—ch" at the presser. When Khamzat Chimaev and Dillon Danis actually went head-to-head at RAF 10, "Borz" pinned him in 44 seconds , so the shirt doesn't make much sense. Still, it was enough to send notorious hothead Arman Tsarukyan apoplectic, and the top-ranked Lightweight went ballistic in defense of his close friend and training partner (see all that here) .

Where was Khamzat himself during all the chaos? New footage reveals that Chimaev was being restrained by about four people who appear to be a mix of RAF staff and civilians! "Borz" was desperate to get a piece of Danis and yelled out, "You don't know who is your daddy b—ch! I'll f—k you up!"

While Danis and Tsarukyan will wrestle (and then probably brawl again) in the RAF 14 main event, Chimaev is also booked to compete. In the co-main event, he'll take on former UFC Welterweight champion Robbie Lawler in a strange matchup that would seem to guarantee another dominant victory for the Russian.
